Night buses will run again on the three valley routes from the first weekend of November, two years after they were withdrawn when the operator could not find enough drivers to cover the late shifts, the county council said on Wednesday.

The buses will leave the town centre every hour from eleven at night until three in the morning on Fridays and Saturdays, calling at every stop on the way up the valley as far as the reservoir. On other nights the last bus will leave at half past eleven, as it does now.

Valley Link, which runs the routes, has trained twenty new drivers since the spring, and says it can now staff the late shifts without cancelling daytime journeys. Each night bus will carry a second member of staff until midnight, when the town's pubs close.

The council will pay for the service for its first two years from a fund for rural transport, at a cost of about three hundred thousand pounds a year. Fares will be the same as in the daytime, and the county's free passes for older people will be accepted on every journey.

People who work late shifts at the hospital, the distribution centre on the ring road and the town's restaurants have campaigned for the buses since they stopped. A petition calling for their return was signed by more than four thousand people in the valley last winter.

The council said it would count passengers on every journey for the first six months, and that routes which carried too few people after midnight could finish earlier from the spring. The timetable will be printed at every stop on the routes by the end of the month.
